name: ESL MPSoC tile/PE array (parametric \foreach generator)
author: cp-4892 (WP-4, ADR-0005 D5) -- extends the esl-architecture-block PoC (cp-4856) with a \foreach-driven array generator
description: Parametric MPSoC tile grid (\ntilerows x \ntilecols) with a PE sub-grid (\pegridrows x \pegridcols) contained inside each tile, generated by nested \foreach loops rather than hand-listed nodes. Node names stay index-addressable (tile-<r>-<c>, pe-<r>-<c>-<k>) at any scale. Proven at 32+ tiles with legibility handled via pelabelmode (blank PE fill above a few tiles) and an O(tiles) inter-tile mesh (not O(tiles^2)). The tile corner-label sits in dedicated fit-box headroom (never on a contained PE) and the intra-tile bus is an orthogonal row/column lattice (never diagonal), per coordinator review. Colors reuse the esl-architecture-block domain-semantic scheme (Aquamarine=PE/core-accent, Orange=intra-bus, NavyBlue dashed=inter-bus).

parameters.name: \ntilerows
parameters.meaning: number of tile rows in the MPSoC grid

parameters.name: \ntilecols
parameters.meaning: number of tile columns in the MPSoC grid

parameters.name: \pegridrows
parameters.meaning: PE sub-grid row count inside each tile

parameters.name: \pegridcols
parameters.meaning: PE sub-grid column count inside each tile

parameters.name: \pelabelmode
parameters.meaning: PE-node text label: "index" prints the PE's flat 1-based index, "none" leaves it blank -- the legibility control for large arrays

parameters.name: \tilegapx
parameters.meaning: horizontal gap between tile boundary boxes

parameters.name: \tilegapy
parameters.meaning: vertical gap between tile boundary boxes; must clear the fit box's own top/bottom margins (~0.7cm together, see invariants) or a tile's corner label crowds the tile above it

parameters.name: \pegap
parameters.meaning: gap between PEs within a tile

parameters.name: \showmesh
parameters.meaning: 1 draws the inter-tile NoC mesh (right/below neighbor only, O(tiles)); 0 omits it entirely

edit_contract.node_naming: generated, index-addressable, 1:1 with contract §1b: tile-<r>-<c> is the tile/cluster container (contract component `tile`), 1-based row,col over the \ntilerows x \ntilecols grid; pe-<r>-<c>-<k> is a processing element (contract component `pe`) inside tile (r,c), 1-based flat index k (row-major) over that tile's \pegridrows x \pegridcols sub-grid. This extends esl-architecture-block's fixed "role+tile-index" naming (core1, acc1, ...) to full 2-D grid addressing so the same array-scale node can be targeted by (row,col[,k]) rather than a single flat suffix -- coordinate with the WP-2 adapter's node_naming derivation (cp-4890) before treating this as the family-wide convention.

operations.summary: edit \ntilerows/\ntilecols (tile count) and/or \pegridrows/\pegridcols (PEs per tile) -- the generator re-derives every node name and position; no coordinate ever needs hand-editing
set \pelabelmode to "none" once the grid is large enough that per-PE index text would collide (see invariants); the PE's identity is still its node name, not its printed text
set \showmesh to 0 to omit the inter-tile NoC mesh entirely (e.g. when only containment/tile-array structure matters, not interconnect)
\pesize/\pegap for PE sizing and intra-tile density; \tilegapx/\tilegapy for inter-tile density

change the domain-semantic color for a whole role by editing that role's \colorlet binding at the top of the file (core-accent/intra-bus/inter-bus) -- never a raw color name inline in a style; keep the esl-architecture-block assignments (core-accent=Aquamarine, intra-bus=Orange, inter-bus=NavyBlue) unless a family settled-decisions record overrides it

invariants: each tile's fit box is declared after every PE node it fits, inside an on-background-layer scope, so it sits behind them (containment primitive, §3a)

the fit box uses the asymmetric "fit margins" helper (top > left/right/bottom) so the corner label always has dedicated headroom above the topmost PE row -- a label must NEVER be positioned on top of a contained node; if the label still crowds a PE after a resize, widen the top margin or \tilegapy, never shrink the label off the box instead

\tilegapy must stay large enough to clear both tiles' fit-box margins across a row boundary (~0.7cm together at the shipped default) -- shrinking it below that reintroduces a label/tile-boundary collision between vertically adjacent tiles

the intra-tile bus is an orthogonal row/column lattice -- a horizontal edge between every same-row PE neighbor pair and a vertical edge between every same-column PE neighbor pair -- and MUST NEVER include a diagonal segment (typed-routing primitive, §3a: "orthogonal, no stray crossings"); a boustrophedon reading-order chain was tried first and rejected specifically because its row-wrap edge is diagonal
node names stay index-addressable at any grid size: tile-<r>-<c> and pe-<r>-<c>-<k>, never renumbered or collapsed when the grid resizes

the inter-tile mesh only wires each tile to its immediate right/below neighbor (O(tiles) edges) -- never a full mesh (O(tiles^2)), which is both semantically wrong for a NoC and illegible past a handful of tiles

above roughly 8-12 tiles, set \pelabelmode to "none" -- per-PE numeric text at that density collides or becomes unreadable; verified by rendering to PNG **and reading it at zoom, not just a thumbnail glance** before shipping any array this size (ADR-0005 D6) -- a label sitting on a node can compile cleanly and still be invisible at a small preview size. PE identity/addressability never depends on the printed label, only on the node name

colors are bound only through the ESL domain-semantic \colorlet tokens declared at the top of the file (core-accent/intra-bus/inter-bus, contract §2/ADR-0005 D7) -- never a raw stock-xcolor/dvipsnames name or inline hex inside a style definition (tools/validate.py enforces this); do not introduce a color not tied to a role, and do not reuse opentikz's ot* palette names for these roles (palette collision, see cp-4856 learnings note)
